Agent (Kagiso Radebe): Next cycle. I've booked a field read and added an access note for the gate.
Agent (Kagiso Radebe): To recap: this estimate stands for now, a field read is booked for next cycle, and any difference is corrected on that bill.
Customer (Megan Scott): Alright, thank you for looking into it.

Customer (Karen Duncan): I haven't had a bill from you in months, and now my service has been cut off.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Hi Karen Duncan, Vusi Molefe here — let me pull that up.
Customer (Karen Duncan): How does a bill just not get sent for that long without anyone catching it?

Customer (Karen Duncan): Yes, same address as always, and the account's under my name.
Customer (Karen Duncan): Can I actually pay this all at once, or is there a plan to spread it out?

Agent (Vusi Molefe): Did you get any letters from us in that time?
Customer (Karen Duncan): Nothing at all.

Customer (Karen Duncan): Maybe. I can't pay it all at once.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Let me take a look. I've pulled the full billing history, confirmed the gap in statements, and reconciled it against actual metered usage.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Alright, I can see exactly what's going on here.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): The meter recorded usage the whole time, but the account wasn't set up, so no bills went out.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): I can see the billing gap on our side, confirmed against your actual metered usage, and I've set up a payment plan to spread this over several months at no extra cost while I file the internal correction for the missed billing cycle.
Customer (Karen Duncan): How much a month would that be?
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Spread over twelve months, about CA$150 on top of your regular bill, with no interest.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): To recap, everything's noted on your file, and the team will follow up with you.
Customer (Karen Duncan): Alright, thank you for looking into it.
Agent (Vusi Molefe): Thanks for bearing with me — you're all set.
